# Cartridge test fixtures

The shared oracle for the Flash Cart rollout. 6502-EMULATOR's mapper, the 6502-PICOCALC
port, 6502-DEV's DB Emulator and `6502-flash` itself all check against **these files**
rather than against each other — which is the only way four independent implementations of
the same contract end up agreeing rather than sharing a bug.

Generated by [`tools/make-fixtures.js`](../../tools/make-fixtures.js). Everything is
deterministic; `npm run fixtures:check` fails if any file is stale.

| File | Bytes | CRC-32 |
|---|---|---|
| `legacy.crt` | 32,768 | `98a4e0fd` |
| `legacy-512K.crt` | 524,288 | `bdaa7346` |
| `banked-128K.crt` | 131,072 | `e0e4f83c` |
| `sample.sav` | 12,316 | `45c4068e` |

**If a checksum here changes, every other repository checking against these files has to be
told.** They are quoted in the tests.

---

## `legacy.crt` — a 32K ROM cart image

What a 28C256 or 27C256 holds: `$8000–$FFFF`, of which only the top 16K is cartridge.

| Region | Contents |
|---|---|
| `$8000–$BFFF` | `$00` — the padding the machine never reads as cartridge ROM |
| `$C000–$C00F` | ASCII `AC6502 LEGACY C0` |
| `$E000–$E00F` | ASCII `AC6502 LEGACY E0` |
| everything else in `$C000–$FFF9` | the **high byte of its own CPU address** |
| `$FFFA–$FFFF` | NMI `$E003`, RESET `$E000`, IRQ `$E006` |

The address-echo fill is the useful part: any byte in the cartridge half says where it came
from, so an off-by-one or a swapped half is visible in a hex dump without counting.

## `banked-128K.crt` — an SST39SF010A

Sixteen 8 KB banks. **Every byte of a bank is that bank's own number**, so reading the
wrong bank is a wrong byte rather than a hang.

| Offset in bank | Contents |
|---|---|
| `0x0000–0x000F` | ASCII `AC6502 BANK $nn\n` (bank 15: `AC6502 FIXED $0F`) |
| `0x0010–0x1FEF` | the bank number, repeated |
| `0x1FF0–0x1FFF` | ASCII `END OF BANK $nn\n` |

The 16-byte tags at each end catch an offset error *inside* a bank, which a constant fill
would hide.

**Bank 15 is the fixed bank**, at `0x1E000` — the part's last 8 KB, which `$E000–$FFFF`
always reads whatever the bank register holds. Its tail is ASCII `FIXED END\n` followed by
the three vectors.

### What it proves

A mapper following 6502-VCS `PLAN.md` §2 must produce all of this:

| Bank register | Read `$D000` | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `$00`–`$0E` | the register value | ordinary bank select |
| `$10`, `$2E` | same as `$00`, `$0E` | a 010A has no A17/A18, so high bank bits alias down |
| `$85` | same as `$05` | bit 7 is latched and goes nowhere; 128–255 mirror 0–127 |
| `$40` | `$FF` | U2 is not fitted, so B6 selects open bus |
| any value | `$0F` at `$F000` | the fixed region ignores the register entirely |

`test/fixtures.test.js` runs exactly this table against a reference reader, so the fixture
is demonstrably able to tell a correct mapper from a wrong one.

## `legacy-512K.crt` — the same 16K image laid onto an SST39SF040

Byte-for-byte what `6502-flash layout legacy.crt --size 512K` must emit, per `DESIGN.md`
*Legacy 16K images*:

| Flash offset | From |
|---|---|
| `0x00000–0x01FFF` | `legacy.crt` `$C000–$DFFF` (bank 0) |
| `0x7E000–0x7FFFF` | `legacy.crt` `$E000–$FFFF` (the fixed bank) |
| everything else | `$FF`, the erased state |

The `$FF` fill is not cosmetic: after a chip erase those sectors already match, so
`program` skips them and a small cart writes in seconds instead of a minute and a half.

## `sample.sav` — a three-sector save overlay

Against `banked-128K.crt`, in the container of 6502-VCS `PLAN.md` §4.

Sectors **0, 28 and 29**, deliberately non-contiguous, and deliberately handed to the
writer out of order so that a reader proves records come back ascending. Sectors 28 and 29
are bank 14 — the highest usable bank, where the 6502-CRT template tells a cartridge to
keep its saves.

Each sector opens with an ASCII line naming itself and then counts `0x00`–`0xFF` repeatedly,
so a misplaced sector is visible immediately.

Applying it to any other build of the cartridge must **fail**: the header carries the image
size and CRC-32, and a rebuilt cartridge moves the CRC. That refusal is the whole point of
the format — a save can never be laid over code it was not written against, and
`6502-flash program` never reads one at all.
